results.summary_before: This design simulates Conway's Game of Life on a 32x16 grid with periodic boundary conditions. It outputs the state to an ANSI serial terminal over UART and also provides VGA output via the bidirectional pins. The initial state is pseudo-randomly generated using an LFSR, and the simulation can be controlled via single-character commands over UART. Silicon testing confirmed that the terminal output works as expected.

results.summary_before: This design computes the Mandelbrot fractal in real time while racing the VGA beam, using one iteration per clock cycle and a maximum depth of 16 iterations. It outputs a 720x480 VGA signal through a Tiny VGA Pmod, with the fractal rendered at 180x480 pixels using 16-bit fixed-point arithmetic and approximated multipliers. The image position and zoom are configured through the input and bidirectional pins, with control values written during vsync. It is notable for fitting a real-time fractal renderer into a 2x2 tile area at 100 MHz.

results.summary_before: This SystemVerilog design produces an 800x600 60 Hz SVGA output with a background and a single 12x12 sprite, internally rendered at 100x75 and scaled up. It requires a Tiny VGA Pmod for output and an SPI master for configuration. The design is deliberately limited to one sprite, as the name suggests.

results.summary_before: This is a configurable ring oscillator built from up to 3853 inverters, with taps at chain lengths of 1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 21, 51, 101, 201, 501, 1001, 2001, 3001 and 3853. The ring is enabled by connecting one of the tap outputs back to the ring_in input, and the resulting frequency is measured externally. A scope or logic analyzer is needed to measure the output frequency and the delay between different points in the chain. The design is intended for characterizing inverter delay and oscillator behavior on the process.
